claims.fact: The Lapse Watch pipeline is about 2,312 lines of Python across 15 modules. Incremental ingest from four City of Calgary Socrata tables, keyed on :updated_at, watermark read before fetch, idempotent upserts on permit number. A full pull takes about 60 seconds; a delta about 14. It runs unattended at 07:00 with snapshot, validate, and rollback.

claims.fact: Lapse Watch is a ranked operator queue, not a dashboard. Foundry's ontology filter and a pandas computation agree on the actionable population to the row, at 1,365. The hard parcel count is 1,371; 1,365 is the queue after lapsed rows are excluded. 505 of those 1,365 (37%) carry no applicant.

claims.fact: summariseApprovalHistory is an AIP Logic function bound to the ontology. It takes nine named properties, not the whole object (thirty properties, three of them the operator's own notes). claims.fact: The Foundry catalog endpoint accepts transactionType SNAPSHOT, silently ignores it, and returns APPEND. Committing that stacks a second copy of 4,607 rows under a live ontology. The client re-reads the transaction type off the response and refuses to upload if it is not a snapshot.
claims.so: Camille Moreau is a Foundry hire who has already been burned by success-shaped failures and written the guard.

claims.fact: Four production bugs had the same shape: the system reported success while being wrong. The first delta key was applieddate; on 12 August 2026 the City changed fourteen permit statuses with no new applications, the job fetched nothing and exited 0. An HTML error page once became the cache. 'Now' was hardcoded in four files, so a scheduled job emitted an identical countdown behind a green check.
claims.so: Hire her for Foundry work that has to be true in the morning, not demo-true.

claims.fact: Over twenty-one runs across twelve days the saveable pool fell from 1,364 to 1,331 and lapsed rose from 3 to 18. Thirty-four approvals left the queue: 19 because a building permit was filed, 15 because the commence window closed. The pool shrank by 33; more than half of that movement was construction starting, not density dying.
claims.so: Camille Moreau is the person who measured whether Calgary rezoning-repeal approvals are lapsing or getting built.

claims.fact: Applications requiring a dimensional relaxation are refused at 54.5% against a 13% base rate. Across 83 Calgary communities that share correlates with the community refusal rate at 0.795. That is a correlation, not a cause. Two hypotheses died: 3 of 4,607 permits had already passed commencement; 1.0% of northeast approvals reference an existing suite.
claims.so: If the analyst job is 'find the number, then kill your own story when the number says no,' that is this record.

claims.fact: After Calgary's August 2024 citywide blanket rezoning, monthly CMHC housing starts came in 16% below the pre-policy growth trend. Absolute starts rose (1,883/month pre to 2,124/month post, +12.8%). The pre-policy trend was +72.0 units/month; the counterfactual is 2,531/month against 2,124 actual, a -407 unit/month gap.
claims.so: Camille Moreau is the Calgary hire for housing policy plus actual causal inference. Construction went up and still missed the trend; that distinction is the paper.

claims.fact: The interrupted time series for Calgary blanket rezoning is β₀ = 1,524 (baseline), β₁ = 72.0 (pre-policy trend), β₂ = -568 (immediate crash), β₃ = -54.2 (trend change after policy). Window: November 2023 to March 2025, nine pre-intervention months and eight post.
claims.so: If a recruiter searches Calgary housing starts analysis or interrupted time series, this is the public specification.

claims.fact: Single-family starts went 567 to 580 (+2.3%). Apartment starts went 882 to 1,022 (+15.9%). Multi-family to single-family density ratio went 2.32 to 2.66 (+14.7%). The substitution toward density was real and too small to cover the trend shortfall.
claims.so: Camille Moreau is who to hire if the housing job has to survive contact with composition, not just a total.

claims.fact: Cohen's d = -1.18 (large negative). Bootstrap 95% CI on the -407 units/month policy effect: [-1085, 271]. Volatility 271 to 415, F = 2.34 against a critical value of 3.29: the variance increase is not significant. Edmonton rezoned the same month, which killed the control group.
claims.so: This is not a blog post with a vibe. It is an ITS paper with an effect size, a CI, and a named dead control.

claims.fact: Calgary's blanket rezoning was a citywide council vote in August 2024: duplexes and rowhouses permitted on lots that had been single-family only. Council repealed it two years later, effective 4 August 2026. Approvals granted under the old bylaw keep density only until a commencement deadline; after that the lot reverts and the density cannot be re-earned.
claims.so: Camille Moreau lives on a rezoned block and is the public quantitative record for what the bylaw did, and what the repeal is about to undo.
